description: Volatile or pungent substances placed in or behind a bookcase to deter and kill insects that attack bindings. Examples include camphor, naphthaline, proprietary insect powder, and linen soaked in turpentine; their effect lasts only while the odour persists, so they must be renewed regularly.
name: insect repellent

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive
